name: The congregation, the day after Korah
charge: Murmuring that Moses and Aaron had killed the people of the Lord
summary: The earth had swallowed Korah's company the day before, and fire had consumed the two hundred and fifty. The next morning the whole congregation gathered against Moses and Aaron and called the dead the people of the Lord. The plague began before the sentence was finished being spoken.
offense: The earth had opened the day before and the fire had consumed two hundred and fifty men with censers in their hands, and on the very next day the nation took the side of the dead: but on the morrow all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying, ye have killed the people of the Lord (Numbers 16:41). The judgment they had watched became the grievance. They gathered against the two men again, and the glory of the Lord appeared (Numbers 16:42), which is the same sign that had answered Korah, and this time there was no test of censers and no warning; wrath went out from the Lord and the plague was begun (Numbers 16:46).
judgment: The glory of the Lord appeared and wrath went out from him; the plague was begun. Moses sent Aaron running into the congregation with a censer to make an atonement, and he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stayed. Fourteen thousand and seven hundred died, beside them that died about the matter of Korah.

entries.commentary: Korah was of Levi, and Dathan, Abiram, and On were of Reuben. With them rose up two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown; that is two hundred and fifty three in all against Moses and Aaron. These were known and powerful men among the congregation, and their influence, because of who they were, is how they were able to persuade people. They charged Moses and Aaron with taking too much upon themselves and lifting themselves above the congregation. They thought Moses and Aaron carried themselves as better than the rest, but the Most High is the one who chose them as leaders and was dealing with them; the accusers were jealous of them.

When Moses heard it, he fell upon his face, and told Korah and all his company: even to morrow the Lord will shew who are his, and who is holy; the Most High himself would show whom he chose and whom he was dealing with. The test was censers: take you censers, Korah and all his company, put fire therein and incense before the Lord, and the man whom the Lord doth choose, he shall be holy. Ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi.

Moses exhorted Korah: seemeth it but a small thing that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation to bring you near to himself, to do the service of the tabernacle? Only Levi could do the service of the tabernacle, and that was a heavy job in itself. You already stand before the congregation and minister unto them; the Most High is still dealing with you. But they sought the priesthood also, and for that cause Korah and all his company were gathered together against the Lord: and what is Aaron, that ye murmur against him?

Dathan and Abiram would not come up when Moses called them. They were being rebellious against Moses because they wanted his spot, accusing him of bringing them out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill them in the wilderness and of making himself a prince over them. Those same spirits are around today; the same thing that went on in the old time goes on now.

Moses was very wroth and said unto the Lord, respect not thou their offering: I have not taken one ass from them, neither have I hurt one of them. Every man took his censer, two hundred and fifty censers, with Aaron and Korah also, put fire and incense in them, and stood in the door of the tabernacle of the congregation; and Korah gathered all the congregation against Moses and Aaron, and the glory of the Lord appeared unto all the congregation.

The Lord told Moses and Aaron to separate themselves from among the congregation, that he might consume them in a moment: get away from them, because judgment is about to come. Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces and pleaded: O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and wilt thou be wroth with all the congregation? They still had that love for their people and pleaded with the Lord not to deal with the whole congregation over one man's sin.

The Lord commanded the congregation to get up from about the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram; Moses warned them to depart from the tents of these wicked men and touch nothing of theirs, lest they be consumed in all their sins and put to death in all that wickedness. The congregation got up from the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on every side; and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood in the door of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little children.

Moses put the proof on the Most High: hereby ye shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all these works, for I have not done them of mine own mind. If these men die the common death of all men, then the Lord hath not sent me; if the Most High does not do something out of the ordinary to put them to death, then the Lord had not sent him. But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth and swallow them up, and they go down quick into the pit, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.

As he made an end of speaking, the ground clave asunder under them, and the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, their houses, all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods; anybody that had something to do with them went down, with all they owned. The earth just opened and closed upon them, and they perished from among the congregation; all Israel round about fled at the cry of them, for you could hear them crying as they were swallowed up, and they said, lest the earth swallow us up also.
The other two hundred and fifty men that followed them and offered incense did not escape either: there came out a fire from the Lord and consumed them.

The Lord told Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers out of the burning, for they are hallowed, and scatter the fire yonder; the censers of these sinners against their own souls were made broad plates for a covering of the altar, because they were offered before the Lord. The plates were a memorial and a sign unto the children of Israel, that no stranger which is not of the seed of Aaron come near to offer incense before the Lord, that he be not as Korah and as his company.

On the morrow, the very next day, all the congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, ye have killed the people of the Lord. After they had just seen the earth open up and swallow men, they still would not let it go and gathered against Moses again; that is just how rebellious we are. The Most High saw what was going on, and the cloud covered the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord appeared; Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle because they knew the Most High was ready to deal with them. The Lord came down ready to put them to death again, saying get you up from among this congregation, that I may consume them as in a moment; and Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces, still pleading for their people because they loved them so much.

Moses told Aaron to take a censer with fire from off the altar and incense, and go quickly unto the congregation and make an atonement for them, for wrath had gone out from the Lord and the plague was begun; the Most High was already putting them to death. Aaron ran into the midst of the congregation, put on incense, made an atonement for the people, and stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.

They that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside them that died about the matter of Korah; so beside the two hundred and fifty three that died with Korah, fourteen thousand seven hundred more were put to death.

Every tribe took a rod, a stick or staff, according to the house of their fathers, twelve rods, and the prince of every tribe wrote his name upon his rod; Aaron's name was written upon the rod of Levi. The rods were laid up in the tabernacle of the congregation before the testimony, the ark of the covenant, where the Lord met with them; the man's rod whom the Lord chose would blossom and grow. By this the Most High would make the murmurings of the children of Israel to cease from him, showing them that he was dealing with Moses and Aaron and them alone.

Every prince gave Moses a rod, one for each according to their fathers' houses, twelve rods, and the rod of Aaron was among them, and Moses laid them up before the Lord in the tabernacle of witness. On the morrow, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds; and every man took back his own rod.

The Lord commanded Aaron's rod to be brought again before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels, to take away their murmurings from the Lord, that they die not; so he would not have to put them to death again for murmuring. And Moses did as the Lord commanded him.

The children of Israel cried, behold, we die, we perish, we all perish: whosoever cometh any thing near unto the tabernacle of the Lord shall die. You had to be of Levi to go near the tabernacle; that had to be your office. The next chapter explains who was to minister there.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

verses.text: But on the morrow all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying, Ye have killed the people of the Lord.

And it came to pass, when the congregation was gathered against Moses and against Aaron, that they looked toward the tabernacle of the congregation: and, behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
And Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle of the congregation.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Get you up from among this congregation, that I may consume them as in a moment. And they fell upon their faces.

And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a censer, and put fire therein from off the altar, and put on incense, and go quickly unto the congregation, and make an atonement for them: for there is wrath gone out from the Lord; the plague is begun.
And Aaron took as Moses commanded, and ran into the midst of the congregation; and, behold, the plague was begun among the people: and he put on incense, and made an atonement for the people.
And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.
Now they that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside them that died about the matter of Korah.
And Aaron returned unto Moses unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: and the plague was stayed.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Bring Aaron’s rod again before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels; and thou shalt quite take away their murmurings from me, that they die not.
Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.
They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord.
The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.
And a fire was kindled in their company; the flame burned up the wicked.
